subject: Island 014 second Blender solid modular honey cathedral facade first geometry gate

inputs.evidenceIntegrity: All four v005 SVG/JPEG hash pairs match the immutable capture manifest; the JPEGs are browser rasterizations of the actual-mesh SVG captures.

meshBudgetAssessment.finding: The multipart and triangle budgets pass.

perViewScores.note: The facade is solid, centered, attached, and all four bays are clear. The rose is larger and more visually dominant than the doorway, while the door backplane is nearly blank: seam, handles, bee sigil, and occupied dark recess do not read in clay.
Closed reveal volumes and host attachment survive the oblique, with all four bays countable. The rose ring projects as a large barrel-like crown and the visually blank doorway remains subordinate.
The opposite oblique confirms solid topology, attachment, and four-bay count, together with the same oversized forward rose and under-occupied door.
The close view proves a substantial pointed arch and closed door plane, but the door is visually blank and fails to express the royal entrance details required to lead the hierarchy.

criticalFloorEvaluation.finding: The blockout clears the immediate-retirement floor exactly, not comfortably.

openHoleOrHollowCard.finding: No background is visible through the door, rose, or bays; closed backplanes and reveal volumes survive both obliques.

blankCentralSlabHidingDoor.finding: The door opening and arch remain visible, although the occupied door details are insufficiently readable.

largestMismatch: The source's royal doorway is the first focal point, with a smaller embedded rose above it. This blockout reverses that hierarchy: a large forward rose barrel dominates while the broad door reads as an almost blank plane without phone-readable seam, handles, bee sigil, or occupied recess depth.

boundedCorrection.hardRejectThreshold: Retire the family if the corrected worst required score is below 0.85, if worst-score gain is below +0.10, if any open-hole/hollow-card read appears, if fewer than four bays remain countable at 45 or 315 degrees, if the rose remains first or projects more than 0.06 ahead of the gable, if door seam/handles/sigil remain unreadable in any required view, if any central part becomes unattached or open, or if attachment/cross-view coherence regresses by more than 0.05.
